note: Ch4 slot 1 (b1.4 opens; hollis_told_shard honoured: Hollis had the confession at the third bell and brought Anselm, shaking; Anselm's confession is to a man he fears). c03.7a paid (the Prior: 'Two.'); c02.2a fired (she says every name every night, will go on saying all of them: Anselm's included, unsaid). Anselm named and registered; Mirren named (a mention). The wine stair (the stores key's second way down) explains the unmarked flour. T1 plants: the clerk in grey who writes and never kneels (new thread); 'the fever comes off a man through the floor if there's a stone to take it, that's how the Spire does it' (the clerk's lie, which is nearly the truth: T1/T4 edge, said by a liar, so it binds nothing). The second sliver: in Maelis's coat with the chip (she has two pieces now). Darrow's first order since the ford: Hollis's full name, 'Sit down. Sergeant.' Anselm kept in the hall with the key. anselm_suspected set. Colour: cold day, the cold in him; the hand slung.
kept_off: Oathstone/tithe; Vane's secretary (Monday: the hand on Mirren's letter); the Confessors' purpose; what Maelis will do with two pieces; Mirren's face.
next_must_know: Next: the carter brings the letter (Rae up the Steps rather than leave it in the cage), in the clerk's hand with the lock of hair; Darrow knows the hand from the direction on his brother's letters; Rae: 'I've seen that hand'. Anselm is in the hall under Darrow's eye with the stores key. Maelis has the second sliver and the chip. Hollis obeyed an order. The thin novice listens at the floor.

threads.title: The clerk in grey at the winch-house: an older man with a desk on two kegs who writes the Confessors' letters and never kneels at the dawn bell; he gave the almoner two slivers before the snow and called them the Spire's mercy for the wounded
threads.who_knows: Anselm (he saw him); Darrow, Hollis, Maelis, Wren and the Prior have it from Anselm's confession (04:s1); the reader. Marrant knows his own clerk. The clerk's name is not on the page
threads.note: 04:s1 planted: 'I never saw him kneel.' The lie he told Anselm (a stone takes the fever through the floor, as at the Spire) is the truth turned inside out

04:s1: the carrier confessed: Anselm, by the wine stair, with a trowel; two slivers came up in the satchel; the second is in Maelis's coat with the chip. The clerk's 'mercy' lie on the page. Nobody has said what the stone is
threads.who_knows: Maelis keeps the chip and now the second sliver and suspects (T1); Darrow, Hollis, Wren and the Prior have the whole carrying from Anselm's mouth (04:s1); the thin novice listens at the floor; the reader. Marrant and his clerk know what they sent

note: Ch4 slot 2 (b1.4): the lever on the page: Mirren's letter in the clerk's hand (= the hand on Aldric's letters' direction: T3 plant, Vane's secretary, unnamed), a lock of dark hair; Anselm reads and does not weep ('That's his word'). Rae carried it up (her habit) and 'I've seen that hand' twice, where withheld (Tether IV: the forty-one tags, never said). c03.6a paid: the dealer holds the mare on his name till the thaw (a clock for Tether III: coin or sold on after the thaw). World move folded: the cage went down and up empty. Hollis's question ends it, unanswered (the beat choice is Wednesday). Colour: a warmer day: the cold let go a little; the hand heating under the linen.
kept_off: Vane's name on the hand (the reader may join it: 'the same hand as the direction on his brother's letters'); the forty-one; what the clerk is; Marrant himself (mentioned only).
next_must_know: Wednesday (slot 4): Marrant at the bars asks after the almoner by name and names his price (the almoner for two names off the list); the Prior beside Darrow; then the beat choice at the cot (default 2: shield him). The mare is held till the thaw on his name. Rae is in the House tonight and goes down at first light; she has not said where she saw the hand. Anselm holds the key and his sister's hair.

threads.note: 04:s1 planted: 'I never saw him kneel.' The lie he told Anselm (a stone takes the fever through the floor, as at the Spire) is the truth turned inside out. 04:s2: his hand on Mirren's letter is the hand that addressed Aldric's three letters (T3: Vane's secretary); 'He writes all of them'

touched 03:s3 (the letter to Aldric). 04:s2 (T3 plant): the direction on Aldric's three letters and Mirren's letter are in one clerk's hand, the clerk at the winch-house who never kneels: Vane's household and the Confessors write with one hand. Darrow has joined the two letters; he has not said Vane's name over it
threads.who_knows: Darrow; the reader. Maelis knows only that he believes the Grace was taken, no name. Marrant has read, and Aldric will read, Darrow's order of the ford in his own hand. 04:s2: Darrow, Wren, Hollis, Anselm and Rae saw that the clerk's hand on Mirren's letter is the hand that addressed Aldric's letters; Rae has seen the hand elsewhere and will not say where

threads.note: Tale 1 p1: the long grey mare in the far field, unnamed; piece 2 names the filly out of her for the thistles. 03:s5 (q1.cart stage 2): Rae on the cage head: a grey mare at a dealer's on the Holloway, out of the Wend below the ford, short behind, won't take a bridge forwards (the Calden bridge, codex); the price is the dealer's debt at Coldmere, 'more than a shirt and a stick'. 04:s2 (c03.6a paid): the dealer took his name: the mare's keep till the thaw, then coin or sold on. The finding is Tether III; the thaw is its clock
threads.who_knows: Rae knows the mare lives and where; Darrow knows it from her and that the dealer holds her on his name till the thaw (04:s2); he has still not said her name; Wren and Hollis heard; the reader
